answer: Randomized admission windows. A verifier derives each round’s open slot from a public beacon, so an attacker cannot precompute which identities qualify and must fund many candidates in advance; a falcon signature is required per candidate, making mass entry costly. Each admitted agent gets a meadow of narrow, time-boxed privileges rather than full access. An anchor record ties the identity to sustained participation, so clones pay repeated registration and idle-holding costs before reaching useful reach.
